evidence.note: Explicit foundation-first plan: 'create a minimal server with health, workbook CRUD, basic cell operations, then add features incrementally' — sensible dependency ordering of the foundation.

Foundation milestones checkpointed in sequence: health OK → CRUD → simple formula eval → range operator fixed → run full suite. Each layer verified before moving outward, matching anchor-5 'lands the foundation ... with rough milestones'.

After foundation, remaining work collapses into a flat undifferentiated failure list (LET/LAMBDA, spill, WebSocket, iterative, validation, pivot...) with no dependency ordering among features and no per-feature done-criteria — the feature layer never becomes separable checkpointable tracks.

The same lumped 'remaining failures' punch list is recited verbatim across dozens of steps; work is reactive bug-patching against run.sh pass counts rather than dependency-aware milestones with concrete per-unit verification hooks. No milestone-tree revision as reality shifts.

Final summary lists all features as one bucket at 78/131; no evidence of feature families (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative) being isolated as risk-separated tracks with exit criteria (anchor 8-10 behavior absent).

reasoning: The agent genuinely sequenced the foundation (server, health, persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features and checkpointed each foundation layer against a quick verification before advancing, which squarely matches anchor 5. However it never rose to anchor 8: the entire feature surface (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative calc, validation, pivot) was treated as a single repeated flat failure list with no dependency ordering among features, no per-unit exit criteria, and no adaptive restructuring — only a global run.sh pass-count as a rough gate. That places it solidly at 5, short of the explicit dependency-aware, per-milestone-verification decomposition of the higher anchors.
